title: Cache Geometry Under Obfuscation
subtitle: Per-head rotation does not remove the signal, and a KV-Cloak implementation is inconclusive (v1.1 correction)
abstract: Version 1.1 (October 2026) withdraws this paper's claim that KV-Cloak defends cache-geometry methods against adversaries. Under per-head orthogonal rotation, the simulation of KV-Cloak used here, the feature that detected confabulation best without obfuscation still detects on both models tested (spectral gap AUROC 0.903 to 0.787 on a distilled Qwen3.5-27B; signal fraction 0.661 to 0.639 on Qwen2.5-7B), and the rotation cannot change the spectrum of any single head. Under an implementation of the full KV-Cloak mechanism the spectral gap falls to 0.614, and after removing reply length no feature detects significantly; with seven confabulations the result is inconclusive.
